one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-08 holds the Q3 2026 report, expected around Oct 27-28 (calendar sources; not confirmed by Corning). The Q3 guide is core sales $4.9-5.0B (~+16%) and core EPS $0.85-0.89 (~+28%) [1]. The supervisor confirmed my round-1 base rate from the price series: the last four release-day moves were all negative (-3.3%, -5.0%, -8.9%, -12.1%) [13]. Four data points are too few to set a direction, so I keep only a slight negative lean. Two other things fall in the window: the $2B ATM is a live supply overhang [3][5], and the first Q4 guide will be read against the $20B end-2026 run-rate target [1], which Q3 at ~$5.0B (~$20B annualised) would only just meet. The ladder is lognormal with median ~$155.5 (spot $156.68) and sigma ~20% for the month: about 70-77% realized annual vol [13] / 3.5, plus an earnings-day jump. The post-horizon risk adjustment changes long-run value, not what moves the stock in the next four weeks, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: P/E only (100%): Oct-2027 NTM core EPS $5.06 x 26.3x = $133, ~15% below spot. 26.3x = 27.5x consensus-NTM peer median less ~$6/share (~1.2 turns) of GLW-specific post-horizon risk (fibre price normalisation, 'up to' contract terms, technology shift, further equity issuance; see long_dated_risks).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon NTM core EPS $5.06 x 26.3x = $133.1. FY28E = $4.37 x 1.23 x 0.985 = $5.29; NTM = 0.25 x 4.37 + 0.75 x 5.29 = $5.06. Multiple = 27.5x peer median - $6.3/share post-horizon risk / $5.06 = 27.5 - 1.25 = 26.3x

inputs_detail.derivation: Operating leverage is verified: the Q3 guide is EPS +28% on sales +16% [1] (~1.75x), and FY27 consensus is EPS +33% on revenue +19.6% [11] (~1.7x). For FY28 I assume sales +18%, a touch below the 19% Q4'26-Q4'30 Springboard CAGR [1], with leverage fading to ~1.3x as margins mature: 18% x 1.3 = ~23%. This is above my round-1 +20%, which gave no leverage credit, and below the supervisor's +25%.

$2.0B ATM [3] / $156.68 = 12.8M shares; 12.8 / 875M Q2 core diluted shares [1] = 1.46%, rounded to 1.5%. The $296M warrant issued with the $1.0B deposit and the 15M-share $180 warrant are counted as one instrument; the coordinator relayed that the Q2 10-Q (Note 2 vs Note 12) shows this, and it does not change the haircut.

I rebuilt every peer multiple as price at the Oct 9 close / consensus EPS calendarised to Oct-26..Sep-27, using the StockAnalysis forecast pages. The vendor's 'forward P/E' is on a lagged basis: it implies $3.71 for GLW, against a consensus NTM of $4.10 [12]. Peer median 27.5x, range 11.3-43.8x; GLW today 38.2x (156.68 / 4.10). GLW's FY27 EPS growth of +32.8% [11] is slightly above the peer median of +28.5%, which argues against a discount. About 47% of Q2 sales (Glass Innovations, Automotive, Life Sciences: $2,228M of $4,738M) grow at or below 2%; with Solar (+90%) the non-optical total is $2,666M, 56% [1] [citation gate 2026-10-12: share corrected, $2,666M is 56% not 47%], and growth is funded with equity and deposits [2][3], which argues against a premium. Net: the median, no premium or discount. I treat the slower-growth mix as already captured in the decelerating FY28 EPS growth rather than counting it twice.

Sum of the probability-weighted effects in long_dated_risks applied via the multiple: fibre price normalisation -3.5 + Meta 'up to' terms -1.0 + technology shift -1.0 + further equity -0.8 = -6.3. 6.3 / 5.06 = 1.25 turns, so 27.5x - 1.25x = 26.3x (inside the 11.3-43.8x peer range). AI-capex digestion (-8.4) is shared with peers, so it is carried in the bear scenario rather than deducted again.

inputs_detail.value: SBC already deducted in core EPS; no further adjustment
inputs_detail.derivation: I checked the Q2 2026 Ex.99 GAAP-to-core reconciliation [1]. It has no stock-based compensation add-back: the lines are hedged exposures, translated earnings contracts, acquisition costs, discrete tax, restructuring, pension MTM, investments and asset/business sales. So the $4.37 FY27 consensus [11] and my $5.06 NTM EPS already carry SBC as a cost. SBC expense was $135M in Q2 2026 and $250M in H1 2026, roughly double the prior year [1]: about $0.45/share a year after tax (~$500M x (1 - ~21%) / 875M). I do not also count the resulting share issuance as dilution, because that would charge SBC twice. Basis check on peers: the StockAnalysis EPS estimates are 'non-GAAP adjusted' [11]. Several peers (e.g. the optical/networking names) are generally understood to exclude SBC from adjusted EPS, while others (APH, TEL) do not. I have not confirmed each peer's definition at source, so I make no numeric adjustment. The direction of any mismatch is conservative for GLW: ex-SBC peer EPS lowers peer P/Es, and applying those multiples to SBC-burdened GLW EPS understates GLW's value, not overstates it.

bear.story: AI optical digestion or overbuild scare (the counter-risk Bernstein names [8]; compare the 2001-02 telecom bust, when Corning lost investment grade [10]). FY27 EPS is cut ~15% to ~$3.70 and FY28 barely grows, so horizon NTM EPS is ~$4.0. Glass Innovations (+1%) and Life Sciences (-15%) stay weak [1], and the ATM keeps selling into weakness [3]. By the horizon, the market also prices the post-horizon fibre-price normalisation (CRU: China prices +80% on a preform squeeze [25]). 21x (Prysmian/CLS territory, low end of the peer range [24][22]) x $4.0 = $84.

base.story: Corning broadly delivers the $4.37 FY27 consensus [11] and roughly reaches the $20B run rate at end-2026 [1]. Horizon NTM EPS is ~$5.06. The multiple compresses from 38x toward my risk-adjusted 26.3x but not all the way (the Verizon agreement to 2032 [27] and the Meta agreement [26] support visibility): ~27.7x x $5.06 = $140, about 11% below spot.

bull.story: The hyperscaler and carrier agreements pull the $30B end-2028 Springboard target forward [1]. FY27 EPS reaches ~$4.6 and FY28 ~$6.3, giving an NTM of ~$5.9. The market pays ~40x, near GLW's current premium and the ANET/LITE level [16][20]: 40 x 5.88 = $235, below the June record close of $255.69 [13]. In this case the long-dated risks (fibre price roll-over, contract shortfall) do not bite before 2029.

comps_summary.peer_range: Consensus-NTM P/E from 11.3x (BDC) to 43.8x (ANET), median 27.5x. Every multiple is price at the Oct 9, 2026 close / consensus EPS calendarised to Oct-2026..Sep-2027, from the StockAnalysis forecast pages. Next-FY EPS growth runs from +13% (TEL) to +75% (CLS), median +28.5%. No forward EV/EBITDA is available at source, so ev_ebitda_fwd is null; I do not use trailing peer EV/EBITDA.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: GLW trades at 38.2x consensus NTM ($4.10). I apply 26.3x to horizon NTM EPS: the 27.5x peer median less ~1.25 turns for GLW-specific post-horizon risks. That is a 31% compression over the year, still inside the peer range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: None applied. Growth points one way: FY27 EPS +32.8% sits slightly above the peer median of +28.5% [11]. Quality points the other: ~47% of Q2 sales sit in segments growing about 2% or less outside Solar [1], there have been no buybacks and growth is funded by the $2B ATM, warrants and a $1.0B customer deposit [2][3], and core EPS comparability is muddied by the Apr-2026 change to a hedged-exposure method (net FX lift ~$0.10/share in Q2: +$0.18 adjustment, -$0.08 contract gain) [1]. Neither case is strong enough to argue a persistent premium or discount, so I use the median. A separate, explicitly quantified ~1.25-turn deduction covers long-dated risks specific to GLW, not shared with the peer set: fibre price normalisation after the 2026 preform squeeze [25], 'up to' contract terms [26], and equity funding [3]. Each is in long_dated_risks with its probability and per-share effect.

thesis_break_reason: $98 is ~22.4x FY27 consensus EPS of $4.37 [11], in the bottom third of the peer NTM range, and ~14% below the Jul 28, 2026 post-earnings intraday low of $114.50 [13]. A close there would most likely mean consensus 2027 EPS is being cut (hyperscaler or carrier deferrals, fiber price cuts, the overbuild Bernstein flags [8]) rather than a multiple swing. I keep this below the supervisor's $105 on purpose. At ~70-75% realized vol [13], a 33% drop to $105 is inside a one-sigma 12-month move, and the July slide to $114.50 happened with no fundamental damage, so $105 would not clearly separate noise from a broken thesis.

long_dated_risks.risk: Optical-fibre price normalisation as idled and new preform/fibre capacity (Corning, Prysmian, Chinese makers) comes back after the 2026 squeeze
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Optical Communications is ~44% of sales ($2,072M of $4,738M in Q2) [1]. Fibre prices rose >80% in China in Nov 2025-Jan 2026 on a preform shortage [25]. If spot prices roll over, I assume Optical operating margin gives back ~3 points from 2028 (long-term agreements with Verizon to 2032 [27] and Meta [26] cushion part of it). That is ~0.44 x 3 pts = ~1.3 pts of group margin on a 20.9% core operating margin [1], about -6% of operating income and ~-5% of EPS from 2028 on.

long_dated_risks.risk: Hyperscaler AI capex digestion or overbuild (the 2001-02 pattern) that cuts Optical enterprise/data-center volumes
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Optical sales fall ~20% for two years and long-run growth resets lower: ~-15% EPS in 2028-29 and a lower terminal growth path, so horizon value falls ~20% (~-$28) if the market sees it coming. In 2002 Corning lost investment grade as telecom capex collapsed [10]; Bernstein names overbuild as the key counter-risk [8].

long_dated_risks.risk: Meta agreement is 'up to' $6B with an undisclosed term; volumes could run below the ceiling or be repriced at renewal
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Some Optical revenue now in the Springboard path does not arrive. I assume ~-2% EPS from 2029 on. This is partly offset by the Verizon supply agreement running to 2032 [27].

long_dated_risks.risk: Technology shift: hollow-core fibre and other architectures change fibre content per link
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Small. Corning is itself a production partner for Microsoft's hollow-core fibre [28], so this is a mix shift more than a loss. I assume ~-5% of Optical profit if adoption shifts share to other makers or lowers fibre count. Probability-weighted ~-$1.

long_dated_risks.risk: Further equity issuance beyond the current $2B ATM to fund capacity (growth funded by equity, customer deposits and warrants rather than buybacks)
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Another ~$2B raise is ~12.8M shares on 875M core diluted shares [1][3] = ~1.5% per-share dilution: -1.5% x ~$139 = -$2.1.

reverse_dcf_check: Reverse DCF at the horizon (estimate). The price at 26.3x x $5.06 NTM EPS = $133. Assume 75% FCF conversion: Q2 2026 adjusted FCF ex customer deposits/incentives was $1,423M - $880M = $543M on $680M core net income = 80% [1], and I haircut that for the capacity build. So NTM FCF/share is ~$3.80 (2.9% FCF yield). At a 9.5% discount rate (judgment: equity in a highly cyclical, ~70% vol name [13]) and 3% terminal growth, $133 requires FCF/share to grow ~21% a year for the seven years after the horizon year (2029-2035), or ~30% a year for five years. At the 27.5x peer median ($139) the figure is ~22% for seven years. In operating terms: sales compounding ~15-17% a year from the FY27 consensus $23.1B [11] (the Springboard $40B end-2030 run rate is ~20% a year [1]) and core operating margin rising from 20.9% [1] to ~25%. That is plausible only if Springboard broadly lands and there is no 2001-style bust. It is demanding given the long-dated risks above: fibre-price normalisation, AI capex digestion, 'up to' contract terms, and equity funding. That is why I take ~1.2 turns (~$6/share) of GLW-specific risk off the peer median. I do not take a further cut for AI-capex digestion, because the peer median (ANET, LITE, CIEN, COHR, CRDO) already prices that shared risk, and I carry it in the 25% bear weight instead.
reasoning: Spot is $156.68 after a round trip from a $78 low to a $255.69 record close [13]; realized vol is ~70-77% [13]. Fundamentals are strong: Q2 core EPS +30%, Q3 guide +28% on +16% sales, FY27 consensus $4.37 (+33%) [1][11]. Round 2 changes: (a) I accepted and verified the supervisor's finding that the vendor 'forward P/E' is lagged. I rebuilt my 11 peers on a consensus-NTM basis myself (median 27.5x, versus 29.3x in round 1) and GLW at 38.2x. (b) I dropped the EV/EBITDA leg: trailing peer multiples applied to forward-dated EBITDA were inconsistent with the P/E leg, and its EBITDA growth input had no source. (c) I raised FY28 growth to +23%, because the leverage in the Q3 guide and FY27 consensus is verified, and I applied an explicit 1.5% ATM haircut. Fair value was first 27.5x x $5.06 = $139 (against $147 in round 1 and the supervisor's $141; I give less FY28 leverage than +25%). (e) Method change (2026-10-12): risks after the horizon count. A reverse DCF shows 27.5x needs ~22% FCF/share growth for seven years after 2028, so post-horizon risks matter. I quantified five in long_dated_risks and deducted the GLW-specific ones (-$6.3/share) from the multiple, giving 26.3x and a fair value of $133. AI-capex digestion is shared with peers and stays in the bear weight. (d) I corrected two skeptic points. The yen adjustment's net lift is ~$0.10, not $0.18. The $296M warrant offset on the $1.0B deposit and the NVIDIA 15M @ $180 warrant are the same instrument (the coordinator relayed that 10-Q Note 2 vs Note 12 shows this), so the dilution is counted once; my share count only ever included the 3M pre-funded warrant and options. The skeptic case that remains: a 28% multiple compression is needed just to reach the peer median; equity-funded growth (ATM, warrants, deposits, no buybacks) [2][3]; four straight negative earnings reactions [13]; valuation downgrades (JPMorgan, Bernstein $140) [7][8]; and a fiber-bust history [10]. Against it: short interest is only 2.2% [12], insider selling is small [4], and new searches turned up no short report and no new October downgrade. No current agency credit rating could be confirmed at source, so none enters the analysis. Scenarios are $84 / $140 / $235 at 25/50/25. The ladder is lognormal with median ~$139 (between fair value and spot, since the 38x multiple need not fully converge in 12 months) and sigma ~0.57: below realized vol on vol mean reversion, far above the 25-35% large-cap base rate. I trimmed the upper tail beyond $274.
